# This practice direction supplements Part 58

## General

## 1.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 1.1] This practice direction applies to commercial claims proceeding in the commercial list of the King’s Bench Division. It supersedes all previous practice directions and practice statements in the Commercial Court.

## 1.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 1.2] All proceedings in the commercial list, including any appeal from a judgment, order or decision of a master or district judge before the proceedings were transferred to the Commercial Court, will be heard or determined by a Commercial Court judge, except that –

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 1.2] (1) another judge of the King’s Bench Division or Chancery Division may hear urgent applications if no Commercial Court judge is available; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 1.2] (2) unless the court otherwise orders, any application relating to the enforcement of a Commercial Court judgment or order for the payment of money will be dealt with by a master of the King’s Bench Division or a district judge.

## 1.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 1.3] Provisions in other practice directions which refer to a master or district judge are to be read, in relation to claims in the commercial list, as if they referred to a Commercial Court judge.

## 1.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 1.4] The Admiralty and Commercial Registry in the Rolls Building is the administrative office of the court for all proceedings in the commercial list.

## Starting proceedings in the Commercial Court

## 2.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 2.1] Claims in the Commercial Court must be issued in the Admiralty and Commercial Listing Office.

## 2.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 2.2] Omitted

## 2.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 2.3] The claim form must be marked in the top right hand corner ‘King’s Bench Division, Commercial Court’.

## 2.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 2.4] A claimant starting proceedings in the commercial list, other than an arbitration claim, must use practice form N1(CC) for Part 7 claims or practice form N208(CC) for Part 8 claims.

## Applications before proceedings are issued

## 3.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 3.1] A party who intends to bring a claim in the commercial list must make any application before the claim form is issued to a Commercial Court judge.

## 3.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 3.2] The written evidence in support of such an application must state that the claimant intends to bring proceedings in the commercial list.

## 3.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 3.3] If the Commercial Court judge hearing the application considers that the proceedings should not be brought in the commercial list, they may adjourn the application to be heard by a master or by a judge who is not a Commercial Court judge.

## Transferring proceedings to or from the Commercial Court

## 4.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 4.1] If an application is made to a court other than the Commercial Court to transfer proceedings to the commercial list, the other court may –

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 4.1] (1) adjourn the application to be heard by a Commercial Court judge; or

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 4.1] (2) dismiss the application.

## 4.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 4.2] If the Commercial Court orders proceedings to be transferred to the commercial list –

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 4.2] (1) it will order them to be transferred to the Commercial Court, Rolls Building (unless the hearing is held outside London – as to which reference should be made to the Commercial Court Guide); and

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 4.2] (2) it may give case management directions.

## 4.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 4.3] An application by a defendant, including a Part 20 defendant, for an order transferring proceedings from the commercial list should be made promptly and normally not later than the first case management conference.

## 4.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 4.4] A party applying to the Commercial Court to transfer a claim to the commercial list must give notice of the application to the court in which the claim is proceeding, and the Commercial Court will not make an order for transfer until it is satisfied that such notice has been given.

## Acknowledgment of service

## 5.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 5.1] For Part 7 claims, a defendant must file an acknowledgment of service using practice form N9 (CC) .

## 5.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 5.2] For Part 8 claims, a defendant must file an acknowledgment of service using practice form N210 (CC) .

## Default judgment and admissions

## 6.

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 6.] The practice directions supplementing Parts 12 and 14 apply with the following modifications –

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 6.] (1) paragraph 4.1(1) of Practice Direction 12 is to be read as referring to the service of the claim form; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 6.] (2) the references to ‘particulars of claim’ in paragraphs 2.1, 3.1 and 3.2 of Practice Direction 14 are to be read as referring to the claim form.

## Variation of time limits

## 7.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 7.1] If the parties, in accordance with rule 2.11, agree in writing to vary a time limit, the claimant must notify the court in writing, giving brief written reasons for the agreed variation.

## 7.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 7.2] The court may make an order overriding an agreement by the parties varying a time limit.

## Amendments

## 8.

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 8.] Paragraph 2.2 of Practice Direction 17 is modified so that amendments to a statement of case must show the original text, unless the court orders otherwise.

## Service of documents

## 9.

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 9.] Unless the court orders otherwise, the Commercial Court will not serve documents or orders and service must be effected by the parties.

## Case management

## 10.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.1] The following parts only of Practice Direction 29 apply –

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.1] (1) paragraph 5 (case management conferences), excluding paragraph 5.9 and modified so far as is made necessary by other specific provisions of this practice direction; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.1] (2) paragraph 7 (failure to comply with case management directions).

## 10.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.2] If the proceedings are started in the commercial list, the claimant must apply for a case management conference –

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.2] (a) for a Part 7 claim, within 14 days of the date when all defendants who intend to file and serve a defence have done so; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.2] (b) for a Part 8 claim, within 14 days of the date when all defendants who intend to serve evidence have done so.

## 10.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.3] If the proceedings are transferred to the commercial list, the claimant must apply for a case management conference within 14 days of the date of the order transferring them, unless the judge held, or gave directions for, a case management conference when they made the order transferring the proceedings.

## 10.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.4] Any party may, at a time earlier than that provided in paragraphs 10.2 or 10.3, apply in writing to the court to fix a case management conference.

## 10.5

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.5] If the claimant does not make an application in accordance with paragraphs 10.2 or 10.3, any other party may apply for a case management conference.

## 10.6

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.6] The court may fix a case management conference at any time on its own initiative. If it does so, the court will give at least 7 days’ notice to the parties, unless there are compelling reasons for a shorter period of notice.

## 10.7

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.7] Not less than 7 days before a case management conference, each party must file and serve –

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.7] (1) a completed case management information sheet; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.7] (2) an application notice for any order which that party intends to seek at the case management conference, other than directions referred to in the case management information sheet.

## 10.8

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] Unless the court orders otherwise, the claimant, in consultation with the other parties, must prepare –

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] (1) a case memorandum, containing a short and uncontroversial summary of what the case is about and of its material case history;

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] (2) a list of issues, with a section listing important matters which are not in dispute; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] (3) a case management bundle containing –

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] (a) the claim form;

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] (b) all statements of case (excluding schedules), except that, if a summary of a statement of case has been filed, the bundle should contain the summary, and not the full statement of case;

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] (c) the case memorandum;

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] (d) the list of issues;

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] (e) the case management information sheets and, if a pre-trial timetable has been agreed or ordered, that timetable;

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] (f) the principal orders of the court; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] (g) any agreement in writing made by the parties as to disclosure,

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.8] and provide copies of the case management bundle for the court and the other parties at least 7 days before the first case management conference or any earlier hearing at which the court may give case management directions.

## 10.9

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 10.9] The claimant, in consultation with the other parties, must revise and update the documents referred to in paragraph 10.8 appropriately as the case proceeds. This must include making all necessary revisions and additions at least 7 days before any subsequent hearing at which the court may give case management directions.

## Pre-trial review

## 11.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 11.1] At any pre-trial review or case management hearing, the court will ensure that case management directions have been complied with and give any further directions for the trial that are necessary.

## 11.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 11.2] Advocates who are to represent the parties at the trial should represent them at the pre-trial review and any case management hearing at which arrangements for the trial are to be discussed.

## 11.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 11.3] Before the pre-trial review, the parties must discuss and, if possible, agree a draft written timetable for the trial.

## 11.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 11.4] The claimant must file a copy of the draft timetable for the trial at least two days before the hearing of the pre-trial review. Any parts of the timetable which are not agreed must be identified and short explanations of the disagreement must be given.

## 11.5

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 11.5] At the pre-trial review, the court will set a timetable for the trial, unless a timetable has already been fixed or the court considers that it would be inappropriate to do so or appropriate to do so at a later time.

## Case management where there is a counterclaim or other additional claim

## 12.

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 12.] Paragraph 5 of Practice Direction 20 applies, except that, unless the court otherwise orders, the court will give case management directions for counterclaims or other additional claims at the same case management conferences as it gives directions for the main claim.

## Evidence for applications

## 13.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 13.1] The general requirement is that, unless the court orders otherwise –

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 13.1] (1) evidence in support of an application must be filed and served with the application (see rule 23.7(3));

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 13.1] (2) evidence in answer must be filed and served within 14 days after the application is served; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 13.1] (3) evidence in reply must be filed and served within 7 days of the service of evidence in answer.

## 13.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 13.2] In any case in which the application is likely to require an oral hearing of more than half a day the periods set out in paragraphs 13.1(2) and (3) will be 28 days and 14 days respectively.

## 13.3

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 13.3] If the date fixed for the hearing of an application means that the times in paragraphs 13.1(2) and (3) cannot both be achieved, the evidence must be filed and served –

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 13.3] (1) as soon as possible; and

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 13.3] (2) in sufficient time to ensure that the application may fairly proceed on the date fixed.

## 13.4

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 13.4] The parties may, in accordance with rule 2.11, agree different periods from those in paragraphs 13.1(2) and (3) provided that the agreement does not affect the date fixed for the hearing of the application.

## Judgments and orders

## 14.1

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 14.1] An application for a consent order must include a draft of the proposed order signed on behalf of all parties to whom it relates (see paragraph 10.4 of Practice Direction 23A).

## 14.2

[This practice direction supplements Part 58 > 14.2] Judgments and orders are generally drawn up by the parties (see rule 58.15).
